mn87:3.11: ‘Our loved ones are a source of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress’?
mn87:4.3: “Gentlemen, I went to the ascetic Gotama, bowed, and sat down to one side. As I sat there, gentlemen, the ascetic Gotama said to me:
mn87:4.4: ‘Your faculties, householder, are those of one who is unstable in their own mind; there is a deterioration in your faculties.’
mn87:4.5: When he said this, gentlemen, I said to the ascetic Gotama:
mn87:4.6: ‘And how, sir, could there be no deterioration of my faculties?
mn87:4.7: For my dear and beloved only child has passed away.
mn87:4.8: Since their death I haven’t felt like working or eating.
mn87:4.9: I go to the cremation ground and wail:
mn87:4.10: Where are you, my only child? Where are you, my only child?’
mn87:4.11: ‘That’s so true, householder! That’s so true, householder!
mn87:4.12: For our loved ones are a source of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.’
mn87:4.13: ‘Sir, who on earth could ever think such a thing!
mn87:4.14: Our loved ones are a source of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?
mn87:4.15: For our loved ones are a source of joy and happiness.’
mn87:4.16: And so, gentlemen, disagreeing with the ascetic Gotama’s statement, rejecting it, I rose from my seat and left.”
mn87:5.9: ‘That’s so true, tutor! That’s so true, tutor!’
mn87:5.10: In the same way, Mallikā, no matter what the ascetic Gotama says, you agree with him:
mn87:5.11: ‘If that’s what the Buddha said, Great King, then that’s how it is.’
mn87:6.3: ‘Sir, Queen Mallikā bows with her head to your feet. She asks if you are healthy and well, nimble, strong, and living comfortably.’
mn87:15-21.3: And because of that he went mad and lost his mind. He went from street to street and from square to square saying,
mn87:15-21.4: ‘Has anyone seen my mother? Has anyone seen my mother?’
mn87:15-21.5: And here’s another way to understand how our loved ones are a source of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
mn87:22.5: ‘My lord, these relatives want to divorce me from you and give me to another.
mn87:25.4: “What do you think, Great King? If Queen Vāsabhā were to decay and perish, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress arise in you?”
mn87:25.5: “If she were to decay and perish, my life would fall apart. How could sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress not arise in me?”
mn87:25.6: “This is what the Buddha was referring to when he said:
mn87:25.7: ‘Our loved ones are a source of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.’
mn87:26.3: “What do you think, Great King? If General Viḍūḍabha were to decay and perish, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress arise in you?”
mn87:26.4: “If he were to decay and perish, my life would fall apart. How could sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress not arise in me?”
mn87:26.5: “This is what the Buddha was referring to when he said:
mn87:26.6: ‘Our loved ones are a source of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.’
